findings.title: $__range queries are split after early interpolation
findings.body: runSplitQuery now passes every target through datasource.applyTemplateVariables before querySupportsSplitting. applyTemplateVariables interpolates with TemplateSrv.replace, and during dashboard or Explore queries that replaces $__range, $__range_s, and $__range_ms from the active time range. querySupportsSplitting then calls isQueryWithRangeVariable on that already-substituted expr, so the macro is gone and the query is treated as splittable. The comment on querySupportsSplitting says these queries must not be split: the backend fills $__range from the time range of the request it actually receives, and a split chunk is not the range the user selected. After this change, rate({job="app"}[$__range]) over several days is rewritten to a fixed full-window duration (for example [7d]) and then executed as one-day chunks, each looking back the whole window. Merged results do not match an unsplit query. The new tests cannot catch this: they stub replace to rewrite only $__auto and $step, so $__range stays in the expression under test and the guard still looks like it works. Check isQueryWithRangeVariable on the raw expr and keep those targets in the non-splitting partition before interpolating.

findings.title: Shard path applies template variables twice
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery already maps each target through applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters) before sharding. For every shard group it then calls runSplitQuery with a sub-request that still carries request.filters and the already interpolated targets, and runSplitQuery maps those targets through applyTemplateVariables again. Substitution is not idempotent: the first pass turns an escaped $$ into a literal $, and the second pass treats that $ as a variable, so a label value or query text containing $name can be expanded to a different variable. Ad hoc filters are applied on both passes (the old interpolateVariablesInQueries call did not receive request.filters; both new call sites do), so matchers are inserted once before the shard selector is injected and again after. The executed LogQL ends up with duplicate label matchers, for example {job="x", env="prod", __stream_shard__=~"1|2", env="prod"}. The shard test now expects applyTemplateVariables five times (once up front plus once per shard group), which locks in the double pass instead of interpolating once.

findings.title: Expressions that interpolate to empty hang shard splitting
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery used to interpolate with interpolateVariablesInQueries and then drop targets with an empty expr. It now filters on the raw expr and only then calls applyTemplateVariables. A target whose whole expression is a variable, such as $query, passes the filter because the raw string is non-empty, then becomes expr: '' after substitution, and is still passed to splitQueriesByStreamShard. If that target is alone in a group (non-shardable groups are queued first, so one empty query next to shardable queries is enough), runNextRequest calls runSplitQuery, which filters the empty expr out and calls runSplitGroupedQueries with an empty request list. That function immediately evaluates requests.filter(...)[0].partition and throws TypeError. The throw is inside a .then() with no rejection handler, so the subscriber never errors or completes and the whole request hangs, including valid sibling queries. Previously the empty target was removed before grouping and the other queries ran. The same filter-before-map in runSplitQuery (line 298) also keeps an empty interpolated expr in a split group and sends it to runQuery, which fails the batch with a Loki parse error.
